reports.title: Franklin Templeton, Inc. Announces Preliminary Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year Results

desk.headline: Revenue up 4% to $2.43bn and adjusted EPS $0.94 beat estimates; $20.8bn of net inflows; FY27 margin guided to about 30% on the call
results: Operating revenue rose 4% from a year ago to $2.43bn, slightly above the $2.42bn estimate; investment management fees grew 4% to $1.95bn.
Adjusted EPS of $0.94 was up 40% and well ahead of the $0.78 estimate; GAAP EPS was $0.72 versus $0.21, helped by no repeat of last year's $202m impairment.
Clients added a net $20.8bn to long-term funds, led by alternatives ($9.5bn), multi-asset ($7.9bn) and equity ($4.0bn); fixed income saw small outflows.
AUM ended at $1.80tn, up 8% on the year; alternatives reached a record $304.6bn and ETF assets rose 73% to $84.6bn.
Bought back 2.5m shares for $86m in the quarter; about $1.2bn was returned to shareholders over the fiscal year.

guidance.summary: The results release carried no outlook. On the call, management guided fiscal 2027 adjusted operating margin to about 30% (a five-year goal reached two years early), a fee rate in the mid-37 basis points and a 24–26% tax rate, and raised its fiscal 2029 targets, including a 35% margin goal.

points: Management stressed eleven straight months of positive long-term flows, with about $3bn more added in October.
Raised five-year targets: private markets fundraising to $150bn (from $100bn), ETF assets to $200bn and Canvas assets to $100bn.
Cost savings shrink to about $75m in fiscal 2027 from $210m, and will be at least matched by reinvestment.
The won-but-unfunded institutional pipeline slipped to $22.0bn, and growth in lower-fee ETFs and Canvas weighs on the fee rate.
Capital use: buy back at least the shares issued to staff, plus bolt-on deals in private credit, real estate and infrastructure.
